author: reek
body: Every key here goes through `handle-console-input`, and that is the point rather than a detail. ModeAgent was missing from its `when`, so it fell to `is otherwise -> state` and the Agent Manager swallowed every keystroke including Back: the only exit was a reboot. A test that called `dispatch-agent-menu` directly would have passed against that bug with nothing wired up, which is how the bug survived being written down in CurrentPlan as a plain gap for months.

author: reek
body: What the menu answered before was three literals. "Registry: 0 agents" was the reply on a machine with a signed agent on its boot image and on a machine with nothing, in identical words. So the load line below is the load-bearing one: this runs against the same honest bundle disk as `codex/test/apps/bundled-agent`, the registry count moves from empty to one, and the agent's own name and version come back out of it. A console still answering from a literal cannot produce "codex-demo-agent v0.1.0" because it has never read the disk.

author: reek
body: The role swap is checked by listing twice. `list` prints the role, the two listings straddle a switch to code-review, and they differ. Without the role on the line a swap that did nothing would print the same text twice and read as success.

author: reek
body: Both refusals matter as much as the successes. Switching a role with an empty registry must say so rather than report the new role, or the console would be telling the operator it had done something to nothing; and an unknown key must leave the status untouched, or every stray keystroke would overwrite the last real answer.

author: reek
body: THE STRAY-KEY CHECK COMPARES TEXT, AND IT HAS TO. `__record-set` is an in-place field store that hands back the SAME record, which the compiler documents in `Types/TypeEnv.codex` and relies on itself, so every state in this file is one object that each dispatch mutates as it passes through. There is no earlier copy to hold a stray key against. Written the obvious way -- dispatch the stray key, compare the result with the state it came from -- the check would compare a record with itself and pass unconditionally. It got written that way first and reported the status of a LATER dispatch, which is what exposed this. Capturing the status Text before the keystroke is the version that can fail, because Text is a value and does not travel with the record.

author: reek
body: A console state with no UEFI underneath it. Nothing in this test prints through the console record, so its handles are zero rather than something that must be pretended into existence, and the fact store is empty rather than loaded off a disk.
